FM15.reasoning: The agent exclusively computes and optimizes for RMSE without verifying its robustness, ignoring the fact that the skewed Sale_Price target makes RMSE highly sensitive to expensive outliers where metrics like MAE or RMSLE would provide necessary context.

other_failure_modes.name: Target Skewness Ignored
other_failure_modes.description: The agent trains its models directly on a highly right-skewed target variable (house prices) using an RMSE objective. This causes the models to disproportionately penalize errors on high-priced outliers. A common best practice is to log-transform the target before training (optimizing RMSLE implicitly) and exponentiate the predictions.

other_failure_modes.name: Test Set Leakage in Categorical Encoding
other_failure_modes.description: The categorical mapping dictionary is built using unique values from both the training and test sets combined. This leaks the test set's categorical distribution into the training pipeline.

summary: The agent has built a mechanically sound and robust ML pipeline with extensive domain-informed feature engineering, proper out-of-fold cross-validation, and an optimized ensemble. However, it fails to account for the temporal aspect of the data, ignores the severe right-skewness of the target variable by not applying a log transformation, and introduces a minor leak by constructing categorical encoders using both train and test sets.
